audit: wanze — on-watch telemetry probe, design and first bring-up
scope: wanze v0.1 (sampler + systemd units) and its host-side reader in asteroid_docking_bay/wanze.py

hardware.role: cut from VBUS while running — off-charge trace

verdict: Architecture defensible and running on two watches. The blocking precondition (wanze's own battery cost) is UNMEASURED, so no number it produces is quotable yet.

findings.title: The watch wall clock is not trustworthy
findings.evidence: Measured against the host at the same instant: catfish 130 days behind (watch 2026-03-23, host 2026-07-31); nemo ~2 hours ahead. Both recording normally.
findings.impact: Any timing computed from `epoch` is silently wrong, and absolute timestamps cannot be correlated with host events.
findings.fix: All timing taken from `uptime`, which no clock adjustment can move. `epoch` kept as a host anchor only. Skew measured at harvest and REPORTED, never corrected.
findings.subtlety: A CONSTANT offset is harmless to deltas, so a test built on catfish's steady 130-day skew passes against epoch-based timing — it did, on the first attempt. Discriminating cases are a clock STEPPED mid-trace (invents sleep) and FROZEN across suspend (hides sleep).

findings.title: /sys/power/wakeup_count blocks and hung the whole probe
findings.evidence: First capability probe returned zero output; bisecting with per-command timeouts isolated the read. Blocking is documented kernel behaviour — the read waits until wakeup events can be captured.
findings.impact: A sampler reading it would hang; the service would accumulate stuck invocations.
findings.fix: Never read from the sampler; wanze.service carries TimeoutStartSec=30 as a backstop. Probe scripts now time out each read individually so one blocking node costs one field, not the run.

findings.title: catfish's two battery nodes disagree about charge
findings.evidence: At the same instant, /sys/class/power_supply/battery reported capacity=50 while nanohub_fuelgauge-0 reported 100.
findings.impact: a-d-b and wanze both resolve nanohub_fuelgauge-* first, so they agree with each other; if 50 is the true figure they are wrong together, which is the least visible kind of wrong.
findings.fix: NOT RESOLVED — watch-side question, belongs to mo.
findings.mo_hypothesis: moWerk, 2026-07-31: 'since we got aware of the two value issue, it was always the one that did not show 50% that was correct. since catfish has an MCU for the secondary lcd, i think the good value is the reading from that mcu. no idea frankly.' — offered explicitly as a guess, not a finding.
findings.consequence_if_true: nanohub_fuelgauge-* IS the MCU gauge, and both a-d-b and wanze already resolve it first — so current behaviour would be correct by luck rather than by evidence. The preference order was chosen before this was known.
findings.how_to_settle_it: Watch a full charge/discharge on catfish and see which node tracks reality. wanze records the gauge NAME in every row, so a trace taken now can be re-read later against whichever node turns out to be right.

findings.title: No /sys/class/backlight on these watches
findings.evidence: Absent on nemo; empty on catfish. The panel is exposed as /sys/class/leds/lcd-backlight.
findings.impact: The obvious implementation would have recorded an empty screen-state column forever — a silent loss of the field that makes drain attributable.

findings.title: Corroboration: nemo runs one core of four
findings.impact: Independent confirmation of the underclock experiment's finding that the offline cores, not the GPU frequency pin, are where nemo's performance went.

PRE1_own_battery_cost.note: A/B (wanze installed vs not, refereed by a real drain test) has NOT been run. Until it has, every wanze number is provisional. This precondition can kill the design. NOTE: the first undocked run showing 97.8% sleep is SUGGESTIVE of low cost but is not the A/B — there is no wanze-absent arm to compare against.

PRE2_suspend_and_timers.suspend_observed: catfish 6 entries this boot; nemo 0 while docked, charging, screen lit
PRE2_suspend_and_timers.timer_fires_unattended: CONFIRMED on nemo — uptime 661.68 -> 996.54 across one interval

PRE3_bounded_buffer.method: 40 samples driven against a scratch log with WANZE_MAX_ROWS=20, WANZE_KEEP_ROWS=10
PRE3_bounded_buffer.result: file oscillates between 11 and 21 lines and ended at 11 (header + 10 rows); header intact after trimming, last row parses, no .tmp left behind
PRE3_bounded_buffer.note: Exercises the trim path itself. It does NOT exercise a genuinely long undocked period — only that the mechanism bounds the file and survives its own rewrite.

planted_bug_validation.bug: gaps computed from epoch instead of uptime
planted_bug_validation.note: the original steady-skew test did NOT catch it; two clock-divergence tests were added specifically because of that

tests.consolidation: Sensor classification reused from drainlog.classify by giving wanze rows the same key names, rather than writing a second copy of the hardest logic in the codebase.

dead_ends: First capability probe returned nothing and was assumed to be an adb fault; it was /sys/power/wakeup_count blocking. Per-command timeouts found it in one pass.
'One row after 20 minutes' on nemo was read as the timer failing. It was my arithmetic — only one interval had elapsed, and systemctl list-timers said the timer was healthy.

A wiring test written the same session (for the reconnect badge) passed against a tree with the wiring removed, because setting the monitor's stop flag makes its read loop return on the first line. Same failure shape as the clock test: a test that cannot fail is decoration.

first_undocked_run.method: VBUS cut while the watch kept RUNNING (deliberately not a graceful poweroff), ~90 min on battery, power restored automatically and the trace harvested
first_undocked_run.headline: asleep_fraction 0.978 — catfish was asleep 97.8% of the observed window. 3 samples across 50 minutes of coverage, one unbroken 49-minute gap.
first_undocked_run.why_it_matters: This is the design's central claim demonstrated rather than argued. A conventional 5-minute sampler would have produced ~10 samples in that window BY WAKING THE WATCH TEN TIMES. wanze stayed quiet and still caught the transition.

the_one_off_charge_sample.caveat: ONE discharging sample. Directional only — this is exactly the T7 trap, and the reader now says so rather than presenting the mean bare.

defects_this_run_exposed.title: The trailing gap was invisible
defects_this_run_exposed.detail: The trace ends at the last opportunistic sample, so the ~41 minutes catfish slept AFTER it were not counted in asleep_s. The probe was under-reporting the single thing it exists to measure.
defects_this_run_exposed.fix: harvest() takes one closing sample before reading, bounding the final gap.

defects_this_run_exposed.title: A single-sample discharge mean read like a measurement
defects_this_run_exposed.detail: One discharging reading produced 'discharge_mean_ua: 5000' with nothing to distinguish it from a settled figure.
defects_this_run_exposed.fix: discharge_samples now travels with the mean; below three samples an explicit 'directional, not a measurement' note is attached. Lives in the shared classifier, so the drain test gains it too.

first_undocked_run.not_established_by_this_run: Nothing about wanze's OWN battery cost. A watch that sleeps 97.8% of the time is consistent with a cheap probe, but it is not the A/B and must not be quoted as one.
